- No selection: `runner.invoke(cli)` → no exception, output "no subcommand, use default\nin subcommand\n" (lines 297-299).

Wait — but does this test "invoke a default child when no subcommand was selected"? Yes, the group callback echoes "no subcommand, use default" and invokes `sync` via `ctx.invoke(sync)`. Note in the explicit case the callback echoes "invoke subcommand" first, then the child runs. Interesting: also for explicit selection, the callback echoes "invoke subcommand" — that tells us about ordering: group callback runs BEFORE the child command callback in the explicit case. And output order "invoke subcommand\nin subcommand\n" confirms group callback executes before the subcommand callback.
